cases.title: the closed set of wire error codes and their HTTP statuses
cases.notes: otp_unknown, otp_expired and otp_wrong are NOT here: on the wire they are all otp_invalid (the precise reason is in the otp.failed event).

cases.title: a code is stored as HMAC-SHA256(app key, "envelope|signer|purpose|code"), lowercase hex
the same code for accept digests differently: purposes cannot stand in for each other
request a view code and verify it: link.opened once, otp.sent, otp.verified, a session
a wrong code answers otp_invalid; the event records otp_wrong
cases.notes: And the right code still works after one wrong guess: a wrong guess puts the code back with one more attempt.

cases.title: a code past its 10 minutes answers otp_invalid; the event records otp_expired
a code is consumed on use: the same code again answers otp_invalid, recorded as otp_unknown
cases.notes: The second verify sends the SAME code that already opened a session (no new code was requested in between).

cases.title: the fifth wrong code locks: otp_locked (distinct on the wire) and an otp.locked event
cases.notes: Once locked, even the right code answers otp_locked, until a new code is requested.

cases.title: a new code replaces the previous one: the earlier code no longer verifies
a sixth code request in the window is otp_rate_limited
every limit is a setting: max_attempts 2 locks on the second wrong code
an accept code is only sent inside a signer session
a fresh accept code signs: otp.verified for accept, then the signing events
the view code cannot accept: otp_invalid, and nothing is signed
cases.notes: Purpose binding. The refused attempt costs the accept code one attempt, and the right accept code still signs.

cases.title: signing with no accept code ever sent is otp_invalid (otp_unknown in the event)
the ceremony order holds: signing before consent is consent_required and burns no code
a 422 is validation_failed, with the fancy-sign code as its one item
